TIL the low death toll of the Loma Prieta earthquake is partly credited to how close to the start of the World Series game it was, with most people leaving work early or staying late for the game.

The Loma Prieta earthquake struck on October 17, 1989 at 5:04 p.m. Game 3 was scheduled to start at 5:35 p.m. at Candlestick Park in San Francisco, and thousands of people were already in the stadium when the quake occurred. Because of the coincidence of timing, it was the first major earthquake in the United States ever to be broadcast by live television. Experts credit the timing of the Series as a lucky break that prevented massive loss of life in the city; key in reducing the loss of life was the fact that many people had left work early or were staying late to participate in after-work group viewings and parties, reducing the traffic that would otherwise have been on the collapsed freeways (initial expectations were that hundreds of people had died in the collapse of Interstate 880 in Oakland; the final death toll from that event was 42).

Explain to me why % of thc is less relevant if there are no turpenes. What are they? If they are so important. Why aren't they measure on the package also?

In talking about cannabis there will always be terpenes, the only time you will find 9-thc without terpenes would be as a synthetic compound. Hash contains terpenes, different extraction methods may result in higher or lower concentrations.

It is also possible to heat cannabis products to reduce certain terpenes, however taken above ~313 deg f or 156 deg c will reduce 9-thc content.

In short, they are a grouping of volatile organic compounds and have a variety of vaporization points. They are also prone to oxidation at room temperature. Drying and curing cannabis, as well as removing moisture, is also a process of oxidizing undesirable compounds.

Terpenes have a wide range of effects on humans, the few studies done on terpenes generally use essential oils, which are a mixture of concentrated terpenes and other organic compounds. Statistically significant results in humans have been noted with lavender, lemon and pine oils.

I assume they aren't measured on packaging for two reasons, cost of analysis and unknown effect on sales. A combination of mass spectrometry and gas chromatography would be required and this would be expensive for most small to medium producers. The production of terpenes in plants is affected by both genetics and environment, two clones would produce similar but not identical terpenes.

Testing and advertising exact chemical constituents could potentially open producers up to legal action due to claims made or results advertised. Producers can reliably advertise thc content due to it's high vaporization point, meaning it won't have a significant difference from testing to point of sale, whereas terpenes could be dramatically reduced in that time.

If a producer were to package their product to reduce terpene loss they would need amber or non-light penetrative packaging and inert gas. The first would reduce sales as the market likes to see what they are buying and the second adds cost.

Also, it's questionable as to what benefit it would provide for producers as consumers will buy what suits their budget, tastes and goals, regardless of what the chemical constituents are.
